[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Global Distributed Databases: CockroachDB and Spanner Style Architecture"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern distributed databases like Google Cloud Spanner and CockroachDB bridge the gap between traditional relational databases and massive NoSQL scale. They provide global ACID transactions, horizontal elasticity, and high availability while abstracting the underlying physical distribution of data across regions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Architectural Principles"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Distributed Consensus: Utilizing protocols like Multi-Raft to ensure strong consistency across geographically dispersed nodes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TrueTime API / Synchronized Clocks: Using atomic clocks and GPS receivers (Spanner) or hybrid logical clocks (CockroachDB) to order transactions globally without heavy coordination."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Range-Based Sharding: Breaking tables into contiguous ordered ranges (typically 64MB) that automatically split and merge, replicating across nodes for fault tolerance."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Data Modeling and Distribution Strategy"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike traditional NoSQL systems that sacrifice consistency for availability (AP under the CAP theorem), Spanner-style databases are CP systems that maintain consistency globally. However, data placement must be carefully modeled to reduce cross-continental latency."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    region STRING,
    profile_data JSONB
) LOCALITY REGIONAL BY ROW;"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Distributed Transactions"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Transactions involving multiple ranges use a distributed two-phase commit (2PC) protocol combined with Raft consensus. CockroachDB, for example, writes transaction intents and resolves them asynchronously to maintain high throughput."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Begin transaction and assign a Hybrid Logical Timestamp."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Write intents to the respective Raft groups across nodes."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Commit the transaction record once all consensus groups acknowledge the intents."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion and Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Global distributed databases allow developers to write familiar SQL while scaling out infinitely. To maximize performance, always co-locate data close to your users using regional locality settings and design primary keys to prevent hot-spotting."}]
